summary: Gérard Colas works in Indology. He served as Directeur de recherche at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (~1980–2018) and held a post at the École des hautes études en sciences sociales (~1993–2018).

Gérard Fussman (1940–2022) was a scholar of Indology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1961–1965) and served as a professor at the Collège de France beginning in 1984.

Géza Bethlenfalvy (1936–2021) specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1956–1963) under Louis Ligeti, working in its Altaistics Research Group (~1963–1990) and later visiting the University of Vienna (2007–2008).

Gösta Liebert (1916–1998) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Hjalmar Frisk, Nils M. Holmer, and Stig Wikander, and held a post at the University of Gothenburg from circa 1956 to 1982.

Götz von Selle (1893–1956) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1913–1914), the University of Kiel, and the University of Göttingen (~1918–1920), where he later held a post (~1928–1945).

Günter Schweiger is a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Vienna University of Economics and Business (~1963–1970) and under Gert Klingenschmitt, later holding a post there from circa 1974 to 2009.

H. G. Narahari specialized in Indology. He studied at the University of Mysore (~1932–1938) and the University of Madras (1939–1943) under C. Kunhan Raja, holding posts at the Adyar Library (1939–1944) and University of Madras (1944).

H. Krishna Sastri (1870–1928) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Eugen Hultzsch as an assistant (~1891–1903) and served as the Government Epigraphist for India with the Government of India (~1920–1925).
H. V. Nagaraja Rao is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He has held posts as a Professor at the University of Mysore and at the Oriental Research Institute, Mysore.
Hachiro Hasebe is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Keio University (~1970–1974) and later served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University (~1993–1999).
Haeju Sunim is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Dongguk University and as a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997).

Haiyan Hu-von Hinüber specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She studied at Peking University (~1978–1982) under Kemu Jin and Zhongxin Jiang, later holding posts at the University of Vienna and as Director at the University of Freiburg (~2006).

Hajime Kitamura (1923–2003) worked in linguistics and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tokan Tada, later holding posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1964–1986), Reitaku University (1986), and the Centre for East Asian Cultural Studies (~1987–1993).

Hajime Nakamura (1912–1999) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. A University of Tokyo graduate, he served as a professor there (1943–1976), visited Stanford University (1951–1952), and directed the Eastern Institute and Toho Gakuin.

Hajime Okayama (1948–2022) specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1974) and under Xianlin Ji (1982), later serving as a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1996–2009).

Hajime Sakurabe (1925–2012) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and Susumu Yamaguchi, later holding posts at Otani University (1949–1987), Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1958–1959), and Doho University.

Hajime Tanabe (1885–1962) was a philosopher. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1908) and Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida, later holding academic posts at Tohoku University (~1913–1919) and Kyoto University (~1919–1945).

Hakuju Ui (1882–1963) studied Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy at Tokyo and Tübingen under Junjirō Takakusu and Richard von Garbe. He held major posts at Komazawa University (1910–1942), Tokyo (1919–1943), and Tohoku University (~1923–1934).

Halle O'Neal is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She completed her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Kansas (~2005–2011) under the supervision of Sherry Fowler.

Hammalawa Saddhatissa (1914–1990) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar educated in Sri Lanka, BHU, and Edinburgh. He headed the London Buddhist Vihara (~1957–1990) and taught at BHU, SOAS, the University of Toronto, and the University of Oxford.
